findings.title: Integrity checks compare stored bytes to unsigned columns (fileSha256 / EvidencePart.sha256); nothing binds them to the signed fingerprint, yet the UI calls it 'its signed hash'
findings.userImpact: A record whose bytes and digest columns were changed together keeps 'Stored file rechecked - matched its signed hash', a valid signature and a verified original on Verify.
findings.legalImpact: The platform's own recheck and verify answers would certify substituted evidence under an insider/DB-write threat model; the signed fingerprint that would expose the substitution is never consulted.
findings.securityImpact: Defence-in-depth gap: the signature protects fingerprintCanonicalJson, but every byte-level check reads mutable, unsigned columns of the evidence and evidence_parts tables (neither is append-only).
findings.reproduction: Signed multipart record R. As a DB writer: PUT new bytes to R's key (new S3 version), UPDATE evidence_parts SET sha256=<new>, storage_version_id=<new version>; UPDATE evidence SET file_sha256=sha256(join('|')), storage_version_id=... . Run the recheck: observeOriginalDigest computes the new composite and compares it to evidence.fileSha256 (integrity-recheck.ts:181-183) -> VERIFIED. Public Verify: canonicalHashMatches = sha256(fingerprintCanonicalJson)===fingerprintHash (evidence.routes.ts:13340-13344) and signatureValid over it -> both true; custody chain untouched -> valid. fingerprintCanonicalJson still lists the ORIGINAL part sha256 values and the UPLOAD_COMPLETED custody payload still holds the original fileSha256; no code compares either with the columns.
findings.observed: No verifier parses fingerprintCanonicalJson.file.sha256 / file.parts[].sha256 or the UPLOAD_COMPLETED payload and compares them with fileSha256 / EvidencePart.sha256 (grep: the only JSON.parse of the fingerprint is services/worker/src/report-v2/content-model.ts:41 for counts). The stored-bytes copy says 'matched its signed hash'.
findings.expected: The expected digest of every byte check is derived from (or asserted equal to) the signed fingerprint: single-file file.sha256, multipart composite of file.parts[].sha256 in partIndex order, with part storage coordinates from the fingerprint. A disagreement between the fingerprint and the columns is itself an integrity failure.
findings.rootCause: The fingerprint is treated as an opaque signed blob; fileSha256 and part sha256 columns were introduced as 'the' digest and every later reader trusts them.
findings.remediation: Add one shared resolver signedDigestsFromFingerprint(fingerprintCanonicalJson) and use it (a) as expectedDigest in observeOriginalDigest/recordIntegrityObservation, (b) in Public Verify / review workspace as a 'columnsMatchSignedFingerprint' check feeding overallIntegrity, (c) in report issuance before promotion. Treat a mismatch as FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH.
findings.requiredTests: Live-PG test: sign a record, rewrite file_sha256 + evidence_parts.sha256 + bytes consistently, assert recheck FAILED and Verify not verified; unit test for the resolver on single/multipart/legacy fingerprints.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable PG + in-memory reader: create SIGNED record via completeEvidence with test signer, UPDATE evidence.file_sha256 and evidence_parts.sha256 to digests of replacement bytes served by the injected reader, call recheckEvidenceIntegrity({force:true}) -> expect today VERIFIED (defect).

findings.title: Provenance chain says 'Public anchor: Anchored' for any PENDING OTS proof and 'Independent timestamp: Applied' for unvalidated legacy TSA tokens (web, native, package provenance/chain.json)
findings.userImpact: The Evidence Detail provenance section and the native provenance view show 'Anchored' minutes after capture, when the proof only exists at a calendar and Bitcoin anchoring is pending; legacy records whose token was never validated show the RFC 3161 layer as applied.
findings.legalImpact: A reviewer reading provenance (or provenance/chain.json in the verification package) is told a public blockchain anchor exists when every other surface correctly says PENDING / ANCHORED_NOT_CHECKED; contradicts the one-OTS-claim rule.
findings.reproduction: Finalize any record with OTS enabled. ots-lifecycle.ts:275-280 appends OTS_APPLIED with otsStatus PENDING / otsPhase proof_created. loadProvenanceChain (provenance-chain.ts:193-236) selects SIGNATURE_APPLIED/TIMESTAMP_APPLIED/OTS_APPLIED/ANCHOR_PUBLISHED and sets otsApplied=true for any OTS_APPLIED; web EvidenceProvenanceChainSection.tsx:229-237 renders 'Anchored', mobile provenance.ts:96 the same; the worker ships the same object as provenance/chain.json (processor.ts:4596, verification-package.ts:3518-3523). For a pre-2026-09-29 STAMPED row, TIMESTAMP_APPLIED exists (written from reply text) so rfc3161.applied=true regardless of presentedTsaStatus.
findings.observed: time.ots.applied=true for PENDING (and for a later FAILED record, since the earlier OTS_APPLIED persists); anchorTxId always null because the reader looks for payload key 'txId' while writers use 'bitcoinTxid' (ots-lifecycle.ts:293, ots-upgrade.processor.ts:692); confirmations never written. time.rfc3161.applied ignores tsaValidatedAtUtc.
findings.expected: Provenance time layers derived from resolveOtsAnchorClaim and presentedTsaStatus on the evidence row (VERIFIED / ANCHORED_NOT_CHECKED / PENDING / FAILED; STAMPED / RECORDED_NOT_VALIDATED / FAILED), and UI copy per claim.
findings.rootCause: The projection infers state from custody event TYPES, whose names ('OTS_APPLIED', 'TIMESTAMP_APPLIED') predate the claim/validation vocabularies.
findings.remediation: In loadProvenanceChain select otsStatus/otsAnchoredAtUtc/otsAnchorCheck/otsBitcoinTxid/tsaStatus/tsaValidatedAtUtc from Evidence and emit {ots:{claim,...}, rfc3161:{status: presentedTsaStatus(...)}}; bump PROVENANCE_CHAIN_SCHEMA_VERSION; update web/mobile labels to the shared claim badges.
findings.requiredTests: Unit: PENDING OTS row -> claim PENDING, label not 'Anchored'; legacy STAMPED w/o validation -> RECORDED_NOT_VALIDATED. Render tests for web + mobile provenance sections.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable PG: insert evidence + custody OTS_APPLIED {otsStatus:'PENDING'}; call loadProvenanceChain -> time.ots.applied === true today.

findings.title: Evidence signing-key identity is a mutable (keyId, version) row: no sign-time self-check, seed upsert overwrites the key and un-revokes it, verify ignores revocation, no per-record key fingerprint
findings.userImpact: A private/public key mismatch (rotation without a version bump, wrong mounted PEM) signs every new record with a signature that Verify then reports invalid, with no error at capture time; re-running the seed with a new key silently invalidates every historical signature under that keyId/version.
findings.legalImpact: Signature validity of historical evidence depends on an overwritable table row rather than a key identity bound to the record; a revoked/compromised key still verifies as valid.
findings.securityImpact: A DB writer can replace signing_keys.public_key_pem and the evidence signature/fingerprint consistently; revocation of a compromised key has no effect on verification.
findings.reproduction: (a) Configure SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH to key K2 while signing_keys(keyId,1) holds K1: completeEvidence signs (signer.ts:67-76) and commits SIGNED with no verification; Public Verify verifies with K1 (evidence.routes.ts:13044-13052, :13348-13356) -> signatureValid false for every new record. (b) Run seed with SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY_PEM=K2 and the same SIGNING_KEY_ID/VERSION: upsert update {publicKeyPem, revokedAt:null} (seed-signing-key.ts:355-358) replaces K1 for all historical records and clears any revocation. (c) signing_keys.revokedAt is never read by any verifier (only findUnique selecting publicKeyPem).
findings.observed: Evidence rows persist signingKeyId + signingKeyVersion only; no SPKI fingerprint. The package signer, by contrast, checks private/public match (services/worker/src/signing/package-signer.ts:74-78) and self-verifies the seal before publishing (verification-package.ts:3744-3748).
findings.expected: Sign-time self-verification against the registered public key (fail closed); signing_keys immutable once referenced (insert-only, refuse to change public_key_pem for an existing (keyId,version)); evidence persists signing_key_sha256 (SPKI fingerprint) and verifiers require it to match; revocation surfaced (at least 'signed with a key revoked at T').
findings.rootCause: Evidence signing predates the package-seal hardening; the key registry was designed as a convenience lookup, not as the record's identity binding.
findings.remediation: Additive column evidence.signing_key_sha256; ControlledEvidenceSigner verifies its own signature with the registry key before returning; seed refuses an update that changes public_key_pem and never clears revoked_at; verifiers compare fingerprints and project revocation.
findings.requiredTests: Integration: mismatched private key -> completion refused, nothing SIGNED; seed with a different PEM for an existing (keyId,version) refused; revoked key -> verify shows revoked signer.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable PG: seed signing_keys with K1, set local-pem env to K2, call completeEvidence with a stub object -> status SIGNED, then GET /public/verify -> signatureValid false (defect).

findings.title: Capture trust-event sub-chain is hash-linked on write but never verified, not append-only, and its hash formula is not reproducible for nested payloads
findings.userImpact: Capture provenance (device signature verdicts, session binding, digests confirmed, trustChainHeadHash) is displayed and packaged from rows no code has checked; an edited or deleted trust event changes the provenance verdict silently.
findings.legalImpact: The 'trust chain head hash' presented as provenance evidence cannot be independently recomputed and is not verified by the platform.
findings.securityImpact: capture_trust_event_records allows UPDATE/DELETE (the append-only migration covers custody_events and admin_audit_logs only); signatureVerdict is read straight from row payloads.
findings.reproduction: grep buildTrustEventHash: defined and called only at trust-event.service.ts:138/220; no evaluator exists. loadProvenanceChain reads up to 400 rows ordered by createdAt (provenance-chain.ts:104-119) and derives signatureVerdict/provenanceClass from payload strings (:132-171) without recomputing eventHash/prevEventHash. The hash line sorts only top-level payload keys (:234-236) and JSON.stringify's nested objects in insertion order, which a JSONB round-trip does not preserve, so an external recomputation from stored rows can fail for nested payloads.
findings.observed: Hash columns are write-only metadata; chain breaks, edits and deletions are undetectable.
findings.expected: An evaluator (like evaluateCustodyChain) run by the provenance projection with a 'chainValid' field; full-depth canonical JSON (reuse canonicalJsonValue); append-only trigger on capture_trust_event_records; package exports the rows with hashes so the sub-chain can be recomputed.
findings.rootCause: The sub-chain was added for concurrency (ET-DC-10) and display, not as a verified structure.
findings.remediation: Add evaluateTrustEventChain in shared-runtime, version the hash formula (v2 = canonicalJsonValue), add append-only trigger, surface chainValid in ProvenanceChain and treat invalid as capture provenance class C.
findings.requiredTests: Unit: edited payload / deleted middle row / reordered sequence -> invalid; nested payload JSONB round-trip recomputes under v2. Integration: UPDATE on capture_trust_event_records refused.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable PG: emit 3 trust events, UPDATE the middle row's payload.signatureVerdict to 'VALID', call loadProvenanceChain -> deviceSignatureVerdict VALID and no chain error (defect).

findings.title: Verify final verdict and integrity headline ignore the stored-bytes recheck: a missing original (OBJECT_VERSION_MISSING) or never-rechecked record still reads 'Recorded integrity verified - reviewers may rely'
findings.userImpact: Public Verify shows a separate 'Stored file: Failed' row but the headline verdict, risk level 'Low' and legal statement ('storage signals ... support the recorded integrity state') stay positive.
findings.legalImpact: A recipient can rely on a green verdict for a record whose original object version no longer exists in storage.
findings.reproduction: Signed record; delete its object version in storage; recheck records FAILED/OBJECT_VERSION_MISSING (integrity-recheck.ts:166-176) - status stays SIGNED because only DIGEST_MISMATCH rejects (:235). Public Verify: overallIntegrity = canonicalHash && signature && custody && !tsaMismatch && otsHash!==false (evidence.routes.ts:13489-13494) - storedBytes absent; buildEvidenceTrustDecision input has no recheck fact (:13425-13471); web buildVerificationVerdict (page.tsx:1532-1640) takes no storedBytes; basic verification original.state 'verified' (basic-verification.ts:244) is independent of storedBytes.

findings.title: RFC 3161 trust configuration is unguarded: anchor/policy absent from env templates and readiness, production test-anchor refusal is a subject-string + NODE_ENV check, policy allow-list optional, genTime-unparsed tokens verified at 'now'
findings.userImpact: A production deploy without TSA_TRUST_BUNDLE_PATH silently records every new timestamp as FAILED ('Timestamp failed') with no readiness signal; a mistakenly mounted non-marker CA bundle (e.g. a staging root) is accepted as a trust anchor.
findings.legalImpact: Low: all failures are fail-closed, but the positive path accepts any policy OID and any anchor the file contains.
findings.securityImpact: Anchor pinning relies solely on the mounted file; the test-anchor guard triggers only for subjects containing PROOVRA-TEST-TSA-ANCHOR and only when NODE_ENV === 'production' (PROOVRA_ENV not consulted).
findings.reproduction: grep TSA_TRUST_BUNDLE_PATH|TSA_ACCEPTED_POLICY_OIDS|tsa_trust_anchor_not_configured outside tests/docs: only validate-tsa-token.ts. .env.example files contain no TSA_* keys. With genTime unparsed (parse-tsa-reply.ts:384 warning) -attime is omitted (validate-tsa-token.ts:187) so signer validity is checked at the current time.
findings.observed: No boot/readiness/ops check for anchor or policy; TSA_USERNAME/PASSWORD mandatory even for unauthenticated TSAs (timestamp.service.ts:195-196), which throws and blocks completion.
findings.expected: Production readiness fails (or ops condition raised) when TSA_ENABLED without a readable non-test anchor and an accepted-policy list; anchor fingerprint allow-list; refuse STAMPED when genTime cannot be parsed; optional credentials.
findings.rootCause: ET-TSA-01 remediation fixed the validator but left configuration as documentation (docs/operations/external-proof-register.md).
findings.remediation: Add TSA config to secrets-authority/readiness, require TSA_ACCEPTED_POLICY_OIDS in production, pin expected anchor SHA-256, treat unparsed genTime as not validated, make credentials optional.
findings.requiredTests: Readiness test for missing anchor in production; validator test for unparsed genTime; production + PROOVRA_ENV test.

findings.title: Secondary projections still derive positive trust words from field presence or raw status (evidenceIntelligence.verificationProof, dashboard OTS bucket, admin records, stale digest-policy doc)
findings.userImpact: The review-workspace API returns verificationProof.hashMatch 'MATCH' and signatureStatus 'APPLIED' whenever a digest/signature column is non-null (no comparison, including records later found mismatched); the dashboard counts ANCHORED_NOT_CHECKED proofs as 'anchored'; admin record lists show raw 'STAMPED' for unvalidated legacy tokens.
findings.legalImpact: Minor; not the primary verdict surfaces, but an API consumer or AI context can read 'MATCH' as a verification result.
findings.reproduction: buildVerificationProof: hashMatch = hasHash ? 'MATCH' : 'NOT_CHECKED' (evidence-intelligence.service.ts:527) returned in the review-workspace payload (evidence.routes.ts:9738); otsBucket maps raw ANCHORED to 'anchored' without anchorCheck (trust-summary.service.ts:126-128); admin evidence-records projects r.tsaStatus unmodified (:293); compareTimestampDigest doc still says nothing validates tokens (evidence-digest-policy.ts:205).
findings.observed: Presence-as-positive and raw-status-as-positive in four places outside the shared resolvers.
findings.expected: hashMatch derived from the live canonical/recheck result or 'NOT_CHECKED'; OTS buckets from resolveOtsAnchorClaim; admin via presentedTsaStatus; doc updated.
findings.rootCause: Pre-resolver projections not migrated when presentedTsaStatus / resolveOtsAnchorClaim / stored-bytes resolver became the authorities.
findings.remediation: Route each through the shared resolver; add a structural guard forbidding literal 'MATCH' derivations from presence.
findings.requiredTests: Unit tests per projection with legacy/unchecked inputs.

recomputeRecipe.inputs: Unzipped verification package (format 5) + the record's Public Verify BASIC answer (package.packageSha256, package.sealKeyFingerprint, publicKeyPem of the evidence key) + optional TSA root CA PEM of the provider. Only node >= 18 `crypto`, `fs`; optional `openssl` and `ots` CLIs.
steps: 0. Package file: sha256(zip bytes) must equal Public Verify package.packageSha256.

1. Seal: const seal = fs.readFileSync('package-seal.json'); const sig = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package-seal.sig','utf8')); assert(sha256hex(seal) === sig.sealSha256). const pub = crypto.createPublicKey(fs.readFileSync(sig.publicKeyFile)); assert(crypto.verify(null, Buffer.from(sig.sealSha256,'hex'), pub, Buffer.from(sig.signatureBase64,'base64'))). const fp = sha256hex(pub.export({type:'spki',format:'der'})); assert(fp === sig.signingKeyFingerprint && fp === publicVerify.package.sealKeyFingerprint). Optionally assert seal bytes === JCS(JSON.parse(seal)) (keys sorted, no whitespace).

2. Index: const s = JSON.parse(seal); assert(sha256hex(read('package-checksums.json')) === s.checksumsSha256); for each f of index.files: bytes=read(f.path); assert(bytes.length===f.sizeBytes && sha256hex(bytes)===f.sha256); every ZIP entry except package-checksums.json, package-seal.json, package-seal.sig must be listed; assert(sha256hex(read(s.reportFile)) === s.reportSha256).
3. Fingerprint: fp = read('fingerprint.json') (exact bytes, JCS); fingerprintHash = sha256hex(fp); assert(fingerprintHash === s.fingerprintHash). F = JSON.parse(fp).

4. Evidence signature: assert(crypto.verify(null, Buffer.from(fingerprintHash,'hex'), crypto.createPublicKey(read('public-key.pem')), Buffer.from(read('signature.txt','utf8').trim(),'base64'))); compare public-key.pem (SPKI sha256) with the key Public Verify publishes for the record (the package key alone vouches for nothing).

5. Original bytes vs SIGNED fingerprint (not vs package metadata): single file -> sha256hex(file) === F.file.sha256 === s.fileSha256. Multipart -> read evidence-manifest.json, map each F.file.parts[i] (partIndex, sha256, sizeBytes) to evidence-parts/<name> by partIndex; assert sha256hex(bytes)===part.sha256 && length===sizeBytes; composite = sha256hex(parts.sort(by partIndex).map(p=>p.sha256.toLowerCase()).join('|')) === s.fileSha256; manifest = sha256hex(same.join('\n')) === package-manifest.json multipartManifestSha256. Assert no signed part is absent and no extra original part exists.

6. Custody: const ev = JSON.parse(read('custody.json')) sorted by sequence; evidenceId = s.evidenceId; prev = null; for e of ev: assert(e.sequence === (i===0 ? e.sequence : last+1)); assert((e.prevEventHash ?? null) === prev); h = sha256hex(canon({v:1, evidenceId, sequence:e.sequence, eventType:e.eventType, atUtc:new Date(e.atUtc).toISOString(), payload: e.payload ?? null, prevEventHash: prev})); assert(h === e.eventHash); prev = h. canon = recursive: null->'null'; number/string -> JSON.stringify; boolean; array -> '['+items.join(',')+']'; object -> '{'+Object.keys(o).sort().map(k=>JSON.stringify(k)+':'+canon(o[k])).join(',')+'}'. Use e.payload, never e.presentationPayload. The first event's prevEventHash must be null; last sequence >= s.custodyThroughSequence. Confirm the UPLOAD_COMPLETED payload.fileSha256 equals F-derived fileSha256 and SIGNATURE_APPLIED payload.fingerprintHash equals step 3.

7. RFC 3161 (only if timestamp.tsr present, which means the platform validated it): `openssl ts -verify -in timestamp.tsr -digest <s.fileSha256> -CAfile <provider root PEM>`; `openssl ts -reply -in timestamp.tsr -text` -> Message data imprint === s.fileSha256, Time stamp = genTime, Policy OID in your accepted list. Absence of timestamp.tsr means FAILED or RECORDED_NOT_VALIDATED - do not treat as timestamped.

8. OpenTimestamps (if opentimestamps-proof.ots present): proof commits to sha256(fingerprint.json bytes) = fingerprintHash; `ots verify -d <fingerprintHash> opentimestamps-proof.ots` (requires a Bitcoin node for a chain check); read opentimestamps.json claim (VERIFIED only if BITCOIN_VERIFIED).
9. package-manifest.sig (legacy/format-4 only): Ed25519 over 32 raw bytes of sha256(package-manifest.json) with package-manifest-public-key.pem; covers the manifest only.
recomputeRecipe.caveats: Step 5 is the check the platform itself never performs (UC-TRUST-001); a recipient should rely on it rather than on package-checksums.json alone. The capture trust sub-chain cannot be recomputed from the package (UC-TRUST-004).
